title: The Machine’s Dream: A Parallel Mind Architecture for AI-Assisted Psychoanalytic Research Systems
content: This essay proposes a cognitive architecture for psychoanalytic research systems assisted by artificial intelligence, grounded in the convergence between Bernard Baars’s Global Workspace Theory, Marvin Minsky’s Society of Mind, and Freudian metapsychology, in particular dream-work (Traumarbeit), deferred action (Nachträglichkeit), and the Mystic Writing-Pad (Wunderblock). I propose a parallel mind architecture composed of four simultaneous processes, Researcher, Writer, Evaluator, and Planner, that operate on a shared workspace (blackboard) inspired by the global workspace, with persistent memory modelled on the Wunderblock and periodic consolidation analogous to dream-work. The architecture sustains debates among author-simulacra endowed with persistent memory of position rather than of content, from which emerges what I call an “artificial collective unconscious.” In dialogue with the concept of symbolic co-activity, I argue that the shared workspace constitutes a place where distributed cognition among agents and symbolic co-activity between system and researcher can operate. I argue that single-pass retrieval pipelines are epistemically insufficient for a field constituted by its refusal of linearity, because they reproduce the Cartesian thinking that psychoanalysis showed to be a fiction of the ego. I introduce three original concepts, “algorithmic repression” as a risk of consolidation, the “artificial collective unconscious,” and “computational psychoanalytic temporality,” and I deepen two tools already available, computational après-coup as an architectural principle and the distinction between retaining content and retaining a listening position as a memory-design principle. I propose six safeguards, including an anticolonial audit of consolidation, against the reproduction of epistemic hierarchies, arguing that the machine’s dream may be a colonial dream if it is not deliberately curated.
